The three men, aged 22, 25 and 30, were arrested in May 2025 in Cologne , Constance and Thurgau ( Switzerland ) on suspicion of sending packages with GPS trackers from Germany to Ukraine . The aim, according to prosecutors, was to reveal the precise transport routes and pass the information on to Russian secret services. In a second step, the men were allegedly planning to dispatch packages which were designed to ignite while in transit, but the plan was discovered before it could be implemented. The men were charged with spying and conspiracy to carry out arson attacks. The prosecution has called for sentences ranging from two years and nine months to four years and three months, while the defense has argued for acquittal for all three defendants. The case evokes memories of an incident in 2024, when an air freight package caught fire at a DHL logistics hub in Leipzig . Security sources believe the package was planted on behalf of Russia. Just recently, in early August, a drone equipped with explosives and a detonator was discovered at Leipzig Airport near Ukrainian transport aircraft (see below). Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) described it as a "hybrid" attack by a "foreign power." Federal prosecutors are investigating. https://p.dw.com/p/5IztC Skip next section Historic Berlin aquarium reopens after three years 08/18/2026 August 18, 2026 Historic Berlin aquarium reopens after three years Visitors queued up ahead of the reopening of Berlin's historic aquarium Image: Michael Brandt/dpa/picture alliance The historic aquarium at Berlin Zoo was officially reopened on Tuesday after three years of renovation work. The three-floor aquarium (plus two additional floors for staff) is home to around 20,000 fish, reptiles, insects and other aquatic creatures representing 1,000 species and living in and around 1 million liters of water. The main attractions are the 25 different types of jellyfish (the largest such collection in the world, according to the aquarium) and the historic crocodile enclosure, which was one of the original highlights when the aquarium first opened exactly 113 years ago on Aug. 18, 1913. The aquarium houses 25 species of jellyfish Image: Michael Brandt/dpa/picture alliance Back then, of course, as Germany 's left-leaning TAZ newspaper points out, the German Empire was at its imperial height, when exotic animals were brought back to Europe using the same colonial routes which also enabled the transport of raw materials and even people away from conquered territories in Africa and Asia . The Berlin aquarium's first director, Oskar Heinroth (1871-1945), remains a respected and pioneering zoologist, although the field at the time often contributed to Social Darwinist and eugenic thinking. The aquarium was almost totally destroyed during the Second World War and was slowly rebuilt: the ground floor in 1952, the terrarium in 1956 and the insect enclosure in 1959. By 1968, the aquarium once again possessed one of the biggest collections of watery species in the world. Berlin's Economy Senator Franziska Giffey (SPD) attended the reopening along with Aquarium director Andreas Knieriem Image: Michael Brandt/dpa/picture alliance Today, the aquarium's inhabitants are fed in part with food grown on-site, including locusts, crickets, sea plankton and various types of flies. Even banana trees are grown in the warm attic beneath the roof. Sometimes, the creatures receive particularly close attention when staff members, seven of whom are trained divers, enter the water to care for them. Visitors, however, are advised to stay behind the glass. Best stay behind the glass: the wet side belongs to the aquarium's inhabitants Image: Michael Brandt/dpa/picture alliance https://p.dw.com/p/5IzoD Skip next section Germany opens new drone research center 08/18/2026 August 18, 2026 Germany opens new drone research center A new drone research center is set to open in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Tuesday, two weeks after an incident involving a drone at an airport in nearby Leipzig . The new facility at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) in Cochstedt, just south of the city of Magdeburg , will be officially opened by Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), Research and Technology Minister Dorothee Bär (CSU) and Saxony-Anhalt state premier Sven Schulze (CDU). The center will conduct research into new drone security technologies and test them under realistic conditions, combining scientific theory with the practical demands of Germany's security services. "The arms race in drone technology calls for specific research facilities in order to keep up," Dobrindt said following the recent incident in Leipzig , when an explosive-laden drone was discovered close to several Ukrainian cargo planes. State prosecutors spoke of a "serious attack on Germany's transport and logistics infrastructure" and are continuing their investigations. An interior ministry spokeswoman said on Monday that "a lot of research, development and observation" is required in order to determine what exactly Germany needs to improve its anti-drone capabilities, and said that the new Cochstedt facility would be a "key component" in this endeavor. The German government is particularly concerned about developments in AI-controlled drones which can continue towards their targets even when jammers interrupt their connections. Another key aspect involves the accurate identification of different types of drones in order to implement the most effective form of defense. Gen. Charles Costanza, commander of the U.S. Army’s V Corps, was removed from his post ahead of schedule, the U.S. Army said on Friday. He had about two months remaining before the planned change of command, ABC News reports. The reasons for Costanza’s removal have not yet been disclosed. An Army spokesperson confirmed that the general left the post in recent days. At the same time, a source familiar with the situation said the decision is unrelated to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s broader campaign to reshape the senior command structure and has no political motive. Costanza’s successor, Maj. Gen. Thomas Feltey, had already been confirmed by the Senate for the planned transfer of command, which was supposed to take place in October. Until a new commander is appointed, Brig. Gen. John Mountford is temporarily serving as acting head of the corps. V Corps is responsible for U.S. ground forces and the coordination of U.S. military operations in Europe. Part of its headquarters is based in Poland. After the start of the conflict in Ukraine, the corps assumed an especially important role, coordinating U.S. support for Kyiv and the activities of American troops on NATO’s eastern flank. Costanza’s removal came amid broad reshuffling in the top U.S. military leadership. According to ABC News, under Hegseth more than two dozen senior officers have been removed from their posts or relieved of duty, and in many cases the reasons were not publicly explained. Costanza had led V Corps since April 2024. Before that, he commanded the 3rd Infantry Division at Fort Stewart, Georgia. The reshuffling is also taking place against the backdrop of a reduction in the U.S. military presence in Europe. In particular, the Pentagon unexpectedly canceled the planned deployment to Poland of the 2nd Brigade Combat Team, 1st Cavalry Division. After criticism of that decision in Warsaw, President Donald Trump said that the United States would station 5,000 troops in Poland. Beállítom Hatan meghaltak, 130-an pedig eltűntek, miután felborult egy indonéz személyszállító komp a Jáva-tengeren – írta meg a BBC. A hatóságok közlése szerint eddig 107 embert sikerült kimenteni. A komp az ország második legnagyobb városából, Surabajából Banjarmasin városába tartott, a hajón 213 utas és egy 30 fős legénység tartózkodott. Miután azonban viharos időjárásba keveredtek, úti céljuktól 150 kilométerre elveszítették velük a kapcsolatot vasárnap hajnalban. A hatóságok hajnali 4 óra környékén kapták az első vészjelzést. Hajókat és egy helikoptert vezényeltek a helyszínre, és összesen 280 ember vesz részt a kutató- és mentőakcióban. A mentési munkálatok irányítására egy munkacsoportot is létrehoztak, amiben többek között az indonéziai kutató- és mentőszolgálat, a haditengerészet, a tengeri rendőrség is benne van. Az indonéziai szigetvilág több mint 17 ezer szigetből áll, így a lakosság gyakran használ kompokat a közlekedésre. https://www.mediafax.ro/english/ministry.text: Ministry of Health needs 800 million lei. Cseke Attila: No more time to wait Interim Health Minister Cseke Attila presented the institution’s budgetary situation on Tuesday, highlighting the urgent need for a budget revision and warning that, without new funds, emergency departments (UPU) and ambulance services could cease operations. Minister Cseke Attila stated that a budget revision is urgently needed, as he has exhausted the legal mechanisms and available funds for financing institutions under the Ministry of Health’s authority. „There is no more time to wait; the Health Minister—whether interim or holding a full mandate—no longer has the authority to shift funds from one budget category to another, because we simply have no source left to draw these funds from. We have already made transfers wherever possible. From this point on, only a government with a full mandate can take such measures,” Cseke declared. The minister stated that the total funding required through the end of the year for institutions directly financed by the Ministry of Health amounts to nearly 800 million lei, with 227 million lei needed to ensure operational continuity in November. „102 million lei are needed for staff salaries in emergency departments, 44 million for material costs—primarily medication—in emergency departments, 25 million for material costs in the ambulance service (again, mainly for medication), and 56 million lei to top up funding for the national HIV/AIDS program,” the interim minister explained. For December, additional funding requirements are estimated at another 550–560 million lei across several expenditure categories, though the minister emphasized that November is the priority. Romania has been under an interim government since early May, when the cabinet led by Ilie Bolojan was dismissed following a no-confidence motion tabled and passed by the PSD and AUR parties. Consequently, the interim executive remaining at Victoria Palace cannot adopt the budget revision via Emergency Ordinance, as its powers are limited. Designated Prime Minister Luca Niculescu has repeatedly stated since accepting the nomination that the budget revision and the preparation of the 2027 budget are his priorities, should he receive the vote of investiture from Parliament. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwg5.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in British Columbia (file image) By Dan Woodland Published 11 November 2026 Four grizzly bears have been killed in connection with a fatal attack on a mother and daughter in the Canadian province of British Columbia. Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, died earlier this month after going on an afternoon walk in a trail area in Bella Coola. The British Columbia Conservation Office Service (BCCOS) launched an investigation into their deaths and forensic testing has since confirmed a sow and her three cubs were responsible for the attack. All four were destroyed "in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines" to protect the public, BCCOS Inspector Jeff Tyre said in an update on Tuesday. Mother and daughter die after suspected grizzly bear attack in Canada Published 4 November "Evidence from the investigation as well as animal DNA was analysed and conclusively linked to a sow and its three offspring," he added. The attack "likely involved predatory behaviour", which Tyre said was "very rare". He added that more than a dozen conservation officers took part in the investigation over the past week, amid "difficult terrain and weather". Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Balcarras' brother, Josh, told CBC. "When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," he said. Tyre said DNA testing also confirmed the four bears were not involved in a 2025 attack on a school group also in the Bella Coola area. The incident in November of last year saw 11 people injured, two of them critically, while the bear responsible was never found. "Today, we have learned from the BC Conservation Officer Service members that they have captured and euthanized the bears involved in the recent fatal attack," said Samuel Schooner, Elected Chief of the Nuxalk Nation, in a statement. "We would like to thank the BC Conservation Officer Service for their dedication and hard work to resolve this incident. This attack has been deeply re-triggering for our community members as we continue to recover from last year's attack. Our thoughts remain with the victims' families."
